definitions.explanation: Describes walking or moving at a fast pace. Often implies purpose or urgency in one's movement.

examples.japanese: {足早|あしばや}に{立|た}ち{去|さ}った。
{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ってきたので、{足早|あしばや}に{駅|えき}へ{向|む}かった。
examples.english: Since it started raining, I headed briskly toward the station.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{何|なに}も{言|い}わず、{足早|あしばや}にその{場|ば}を{離|はな}れた。
examples.english: Without saying anything, she hurriedly left the scene.

notes:
USAGE:
Typically used with verbs of movement such as {歩|ある}く (walk), {去|さ}る (leave), {通|とお}り{過|す}ぎる (pass by), {向|む}かう (head toward). The adverbial に is essential — {足早|あしばや} alone functions as a na-adjective or noun.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {足早|あしばや}に{歩|ある}く (walk briskly)
- {足早|あしばや}に{立|た}ち{去|さ}る (leave hurriedly)
- {足早|あしばや}に{通|とお}り{過|す}ぎる (pass by quickly)
- {足早|あしばや}に{向|む}かう (head somewhere briskly)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {急|いそ}いで: hurriedly — more general; can apply to any action, not just walking
- {早足|はやあし}で: at a fast pace — similar meaning but used as a noun with で
